articles.title: Anatomic Classifications and Functional Outcomes in Preaxial Polydactyly of the Hand.
articles.authors: Gonzalez-Zapata D, Martinez-Alvarez S, Galan-Olleros M, Arias-Martinez P, Lorie NS, Vara-Patudo I, et al.
articles.population: Children with preaxial polydactyly of the thumb treated surgically
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, joint alignment, joint stability, JSSH and Rotterdam functional scores, need for reoperation
articles.take_home: Surgical treatment of preaxial polydactyly (extra thumb) generally produced good or excellent results in most children, with preserved joint stability and good movement in most cases. The JK classification system helped identify finer differences between cases that might affect outcomes, though larger studies are needed to confirm this.

articles.title: Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK) in children and adolescents : an analysis of 655 knees according to the CPAK classification.
articles.authors: Pott H, Savov P, Stauss R, Chen DB, MacDessi SJ, Ettinger M
articles.study_type: Cross-sectional analysis using CT scan measurements
articles.population: Children and adolescents aged 4 to 18 years
articles.outcomes: Hip-knee-ankle angle and joint line obliquity measurements classified using the CPAK system
articles.take_home: As children grow from 4 to 18 years old, their overall knee alignment stays relatively stable, but the angle of their knee joint line changes noticeably. Most children and adolescents fall into the most common knee alignment pattern (CPAK type III).

articles.title: A 14% Rate of Surgery in Modern Rigo Cheneau Bracing for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: In-Brace Correction and Brace Wear Contribute to Treatment Success.
articles.authors: Brown MW, Park AM, Elfilali MM, Gorman DC, Yu Y, Roye BD, et al.
articles.population: Skeletally immature patients aged 10 to 18 years with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and major curve of 20 to 40 degrees
articles.outcomes: 72% achieved treatment success (curve change of 5 degrees or less); 86% avoided surgery; patients with in-brace correction of 45% or more had 88% success rate versus 41% in those with lower correction
articles.take_home: Rigo Cheneau braces prevented surgery in 86% of adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis and achieved stable curves in 72%. Better results occurred when the brace corrected the curve by 45% or more and when patients wore the brace for at least 12 hours daily.

articles.title: Long-term functional decline following upper limb botulinum toxin injections in children with unilateral cerebral palsy: A preliminary retrospective 5-year follow-up case-control study.
articles.authors: Tabard-Fougere A, Bonnefoy-Mazure A, Louis S, Armand S, De Coulon G, Vazquez O
articles.population: Children aged 5-12 years with unilateral spastic cerebral palsy
articles.sample_size: 11 patients (5 receiving botulinum toxin A plus physiotherapy, 6 receiving physiotherapy alone)
articles.outcomes: Change in Assisting Hand Assessment score, wrist extension and forearm supination during functional tasks, measured over at least 3 years
articles.take_home: Children who received botulinum toxin injections combined with physiotherapy showed worsening hand function over 5 years, whilst children who had physiotherapy alone maintained or improved their function. The study suggests botulinum toxin treatment may harm long-term motor control in children with cerebral palsy, though the small number of patients means these findings need confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: A bibliometric analysis of research on developmental dysplasia of the hip (2000-2025): Trends, leading contributors, impact, and collaboration patterns.
articles.authors: Kocak M, Korkusuz F, Kapicioglu MIS, Omeroglu H
articles.population: Developmental dysplasia of the hip research publications indexed in Web of Science from 2000 to 2025
articles.outcomes: Publication trends, citation metrics, author and institutional collaboration networks, leading journals, and research themes
articles.take_home: Research into developmental dysplasia of the hip has grown substantially over the past 25 years, with North American and Western European researchers leading the field through strong international collaboration and publishing in high-impact journals. Quality of research and global partnerships appear more important than publication volume for scientific influence.

articles.title: Is D-Dimer Associated With Disease Severity and Contralateral Slip Risk in Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis?
articles.authors: Kurk MB, Albayrak K, Aydin A, Kayis G, Akpinar E
articles.population: Children with slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) compared with age- and sex-matched obese and healthy control groups
articles.outcomes: D-dimer levels, disease severity, contralateral slip development, correlation with clinical and radiographic parameters, predictive model performance for contralateral slip
articles.take_home: D-dimer levels were higher in SCFE patients and were associated with disease severity and the risk of developing a slip in the other hip. Adding D-dimer to existing clinical measures improved prediction of contralateral slip, though the improvement was modest and not statistically significant.

articles.title: Evidence based interventions for bipolar disorder across phases and age groups: living umbrella review, evaluation, analysis, and communication hub (U-REACH) project.
articles.authors: De Prisco M, Oliva V, Miola A, Fornaro M, Dragioti E, Croatto G, et al.
articles.study_type: Living umbrella review and systematic evaluation of systematic reviews with meta-analyses
articles.population: People with bipolar disorder across all age groups (children, adolescents, and adults) in all mood phases
articles.sample_size: 77 included studies (21 network meta-analyses and 56 pairwise meta-analyses) covering 116 unique treatments
articles.outcomes: Efficacy and safety outcomes across 2510 meta-analyses for pharmacological, psychological, brain stimulation, nutraceutical and circadian rhythm treatments in acute depression, mania, mixed episodes and maintenance phases
articles.take_home: This comprehensive review identified which bipolar disorder treatments work best for different age groups and different mood phases, with results available on a free online platform to help patients and doctors make personalised treatment decisions. The evidence quality varies considerably across treatments and outcomes, with some treatments working across multiple phases whilst others are only effective for specific mood states.

articles.title: Examining Sex-Based Inequities in Pediatric Sports Medicine Research: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Sonnier JH, Patel NM, Watson SL, Gippo I, Lew L, Durudogan EH, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of published research articles
articles.population: Pediatric athletes in sports medicine research
articles.outcomes: Sex-based representation of male and female athletes in study populations; analysis of inclusion patterns across study designs and sports types
articles.take_home: Female athletes are significantly underrepresented in paediatric sports medicine research, making up only 36% of participants on average compared to 64% male athletes, particularly in single-sport studies and higher-quality research designs. This underrepresentation means we know less about female athletes' injuries, recovery and return to sport outcomes.

articles.title: Postoperative displacement as a predictor of early elbow motion limitation following fixation of pediatric lateral condyle fractures.
articles.authors: Choi SW, Hwang JK, Kang SM, Park BG
articles.population: Children aged 5.4 years on average who had surgery for lateral condyle fractures of the elbow
articles.outcomes: Early elbow motion limitation (range of motion less than 140 degrees within the first year)
articles.take_home: Children whose bones moved slightly after surgery (1 millimetre or more) were more likely to have restricted elbow movement in the first year compared to those with minimal movement. Surgeons should try to minimise bone displacement during surgery to help children regain normal elbow motion.

articles.title: Comparing the outcome of pediatric femoral neck fracture between Ti-Robot surgery and traditional surgery.
articles.authors: Ma Y, Yang H, Xu Y, Fangyu Liu, Liao W, Bian Z, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 3 to 16 years with femoral neck fractures
articles.outcomes: Screw placement accuracy, radiation exposure, operative time, blood loss, fracture healing time, complication rates, and hip function scores
articles.take_home: Robot-assisted surgery improved the accuracy of screw placement and reduced radiation exposure compared to traditional surgery in children with femoral neck fractures. However, there were no meaningful differences in actual healing times, complications, or long-term hip function between the two approaches.
